authentication_notes: /login returns JWT used for all auth_required endpoints; /register and /users are public but may leak sensitive data without auth; admin endpoints require elevated role verification
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: POST /register must precede any user-specific operations (PATCH /users/{id}, POST /users/{id}/verify, etc.)
POST /login must precede all authenticated operations (GET /profile, POST /reports, GET /reports, etc.)
POST /admin/register and related admin endpoints require an existing admin session (POST /login with admin credentials)
PATCH /technician/reports/{id}/external depends on the existence of a report created via POST /reports
PUT /admin/users/{id}/role and PUT /admin/technicians/{id}/categories depend on prior user/technician creation via admin endpoints

risks: Public endpoints (/users, /reports/active, /categories, /external-company*) may expose sensitive user or company data without authentication.
Verification flow lacks explicit error handling for expired codes or multiple attempts in documentation.
Admin endpoints do not specify required role claims beyond 'auth_required', risking privilege escalation if JWT validation is weak.
Technician and Officer endpoints share similar paths but different tags; client must enforce role-based routing to prevent unauthorized access.
External company assignment (/technician/reports/{id}/external) lacks documentation on external maintainer verification or approval workflow.
